lesson: Generalized Petersen graphs GP(n/2, k) always close an 8-cycle when 2*k = n/2 or k = 2. Steps must avoid divisors of cycle lengths.
Uniform constant chord offsets k create 4-cycles whenever 2*k = 4 or n-4, and 8-cycles whenever 2*k = 8. Chords must be non-uniform or affine-permuted.

Any abelian group Cayley graph with generators a, b has a*b*a^(-1)*b^(-1) = 1, inevitably creating 4-cycles. Only non-abelian groups (e.g., A_4, S_4, dihedral with careful odd reflections) can have girth >= 5.

Every cycle in a bipartite graph has even length. Since bipartite cubic graphs have only even cycles, eliminating C4 and C8 is extraordinarily constrained; non-bipartite graphs provide vastly greater room to avoid 2^k cycles.

failure_mode: High-degree vertex adjacency and low cubic density
lesson: By Bisch's formally verified Lean 4 theorems, every minimal counterexample satisfies |V3| >= (2/3)|V|, vertices of degree >= 4 form an independent set, and every vertex has a neighbour of degree exactly 3. Any search over non-cubic graphs must enforce that degree >= 4 vertices are adjacent only to cubic vertices. Note the bound does NOT prove a minimal counterexample is cubic, so restricting to cubic graphs is a heuristic, not a consequence.

failure_mode: Proposing constructions at orders that are provably empty
lesson: f(k) is the order of the smallest cubic graph with no cycle of length 2^m for any m <= k. f(2) = 10 (Petersen) and f(3) = 24 (Markstroem) are exact, and 54 <= f(4) <= 78. Since any counterexample on n >= 16 vertices is in particular {C4, C8, C16}-free, f(4) >= 54 means a cubic counterexample needs at least 54 vertices. Constructions targeting n <= 52 propose something that provably does not exist.

failure_mode: Searching graphs of large minimum degree
lesson: Liu and Montgomery proved the conjecture true whenever the minimum degree exceeds an absolute constant, which also disproved the stronger Erdos-Gyarfas conjecture. A counterexample can only have very small minimum degree, so degree 3 is the only viable target.

Closing f(4) in [54, 78] only requires a cubic graph with no C4, C8 or C16; 32-cycles are allowed. That is strictly easier than a counterexample, which must avoid every power of two up to n, and it is an open published gap. Score the two objectives separately: the swarm takes --max-length 16 for f(4) and 32 for the counterexample target.

failure_mode: Trusting a published construction without recounting it
lesson: Garcia (2026) showed the lemma under Exoo's 450-vertex f(5) construction is false: the Tutte-Coxeter graph contains 8-cycles alternating between outer and chord edges, and the graph as specified contains 32-cycles.
